title: The Hidden AI Engine Inside .NET 10: WebAuthn, Passkeys, Diagnostics & How AI Really Fits Into ASP.NET Core

entities.name: .NET
entities.quote: inside net ten there's now an AI engine quietly shaping the way your apps think

quotes.text: Instead of being an optional side project you bolt on later, the platform now makes it easier to plug AI into your app directly. This doesn't mean every project ships with intelligence by default, but the hooks are there.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Balanced description of what AI integration in .NET 10 really means.

quotes.text: The benefit comes not from the act of logging in, but from recognizing whether that login fits within a broader, trusted rhythm.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes authentication events as security signals.

quotes.text: For years, logs were reactive something you dug through after a crash, hoping that one of thousands of lines contained the answer. The newer tooling is designed to move earlier in the cycle.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the shift from reactive logging to predictive diagnostics.

quotes.text: Minimal API validation is that door check. Open API is the real time record of what was accepted and how it fits into the build.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear analogy for how validation and OpenAPI work together.

quotes.text: Productivity doesn't just come from cutting lines of code. It comes from reducing the gaswork about whether each layer of your app is speaking the same language.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines developer productivity as alignment across layers.

chapters.title: The AI engine hiding in plain sight
Security that talks to the AI: WebAuthn and passkeys
Blazor, APIs and the self-documenting web

takeaways: .NET 10 lowers the barrier to adding AI by letting AI services plug in through familiar middleware and dependency patterns, but only when you opt in.
WebAuthn and passkey events become valuable security signals when routed into the same telemetry pipeline as performance data.
Minimal API validation, automatic OpenAPI generation and Blazor's typed components turn APIs into self-documenting contracts that reduce front-end/back-end drift.
hook: ASP.NET Core developers hear a lot about AI in .NET 10 but rarely what is real and what is opt-in. This episode explains how AI hooks, passkeys, predictive diagnostics, orchestration and self-documenting APIs fit together, and which features are safe to adopt now.
